situation: A color theorist is demonstrating the complete absence of light to a student using a series of nested boxes.
subject: the darkest colour
brief: In a brightly lit laboratory, a student peers into the center of a nested set of paper-cut boxes that graduate from light grey to deep charcoal. The innermost central box has its entire interior lined with a solid, light-absorbing pigment, creating a void so dark it appears as a flat, absolute hole in the center of the delicate paper model.
prompt: In a brightly lit laboratory, a student peers into the center of a nested set of paper-cut boxes that graduate from light grey to deep charcoal. The innermost central box has its entire interior lined with a solid, light-absorbing pigment, creating a void so dark it appears as a flat, absolute hole in the center of the delicate paper model. layered cut paper filling the whole frame, real depth between the layers, crisp cast shadows, visibly fibrous card and translucent tissue, raking side light. Never a box, a shadow-box or a picture frame around the scene — the paper IS the world, not an object sitting inside one. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
